How the NBA playoff simulator works

Every game on the 2026-27 schedule is played out 10,000 times. A game that is already final keeps its real result. Every other game is decided by NBA Forecasting V1, the frozen model behind these pages: an Elo rating replayed game by game, the opponent adjusted scoring margin, rest and back to backs. A scheduled game carries the forecast for its own date, so a club on the second night of a back to back is rated that way.

That model is not the game simulator. The simulator plays possessions and produces a box score, and on an untouched 2025-26 season it scored a Brier of 0.24021 at picking winners. The forecast layer scored 0.20603 over the same 1,231 games, walk forward, having been frozen before that season started. Lower is better, and 0.25 is a coin flip. So the odds here come from the forecast and the NBA Simulator keeps the job it is better at.

The 2026-27 NBA playoff format

Each conference sends six teams straight to the playoffs. The teams that finish seventh through tenth play the play-in tournament: seven hosts eight and the winner takes the 7 seed, nine hosts ten and the loser goes home, and the loser of seven against eight hosts the winner of nine against ten for the 8 seed. The first round is 1 against 8, 4 against 5, 2 against 7 and 3 against 6, the bracket stays fixed, and every series is best of seven with home court to the team with the better regular season record, played at the higher seed in games one, two, five and seven.

How accurate is it

The model that sets these probabilities was frozen before the 2025-26 season and then scored once on it: Brier 0.20603, log loss 0.59947, and the winner called correctly in 68.97% of 1,231 games. The game simulator scored 0.24021 on the same season and a coin flip scores 0.25000. No number here was tuned on that season, which is what makes it a test rather than a fit.

Tiebreakers

Ties in the standings are settled by head to head winning percentage between the tied teams, then by a random draw. The NBA's later steps, division record, conference record and record against playoff teams, are not applied. Across thousands of simulated seasons they change a seed rarely, and they are listed here rather than approximated.

What the projection does not know

The model rates teams on results already played. A trade, a signing or an injury changes a team's rating only once games are played with it, so early in the season a team that rebuilt over the summer is rated on the roster it had. The win probability for a game in March does not know rest, back to backs or who sits that night. The model data was last built Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 11:23 PM PT.

NBA Playoff Simulator FAQ

How does the NBA playoff simulator work?

It plays out the rest of the 2026-27 regular season, seeds each conference with the real NBA format, plays the play-in tournament, and then plays every series game by game, best of seven, with home court to the better regular season team. It repeats that 10,000 times and counts how often each team reaches each round.

How is the NBA play-in tournament simulated?

Seven hosts eight for the 7 seed, nine hosts ten to stay alive, and the loser of seven against eight hosts the winner of nine against ten for the 8 seed. Each game uses the same win probability as any other game between those teams at that arena.

Who is favored to win the NBA title?

In the current projection the Oklahoma City Thunder win it 29% of the time, ahead of the Boston Celtics at 21%. Those numbers move as results come in.

Why does the simulated bracket change each time?

A single bracket is one season out of thousands. The odds table is the summary of all of them; the bracket shows what one of those seasons looked like.

Is it free?

The published odds and bracket are free to read with no account. Running your own set needs a free account and uses the daily free simulator run.
